Batching and cache tuning results + observed regression

Customer (Elena) to share exact rollout timeline (when settings changed) plus Grafana screenshots for p95/p99 and 5xx for us-east-1 vs eu-west-1.

summary: Northbridge shared results from their Optimize POC tuning (batching and prefix/KV caching). Enabling a more aggressive batching heuristic plus cache toggle improved cost but caused a latency regression (p95 up) and timeouts in one region; they also had confusion about which scope the change applied to. They requested a fast rollback mechanism with clear semantics (who/what/when, one click, and audit trail) and asked how Redwood will gate risky changes (SLO metrics, optional eval gates for quantization). Redwood clarified current workaround options (manual pin/revert) and previewed upcoming versioned optimization config + safe apply + rollback workflow. Agreed to exchange logs/metrics, define minimal quality checks, and align on RBAC/audit requirements to unblock procurement.
questions: Can we roll back only eu-west-1 without touching us-east-1, and is that guaranteed not to leave mixed worker states?
When you say rollback is ‘one click’, does that mean immediate across all pods/workers or best-effort with progress tracking?
Will audit logs include old_version/new_version, actor identity, request ID, and the exact scope (tenant/model/region)?
Can we require an approval / restricted role to perform rollback during incidents (RBAC)?
Can you expose active config version in response headers for debugging during POC?
transcript:
Fireflies.ai Transcript

Title: Northbridge Analytics - POC check-in: optimization tuning + rollback
Date: 2026-01-14
Time: 9:00 AM PT (recorded)
Duration: 46 minutes

Attendees
- Colin O'Donnell (Redwood Inference, Solutions Engineering)
- Paula Mendes (Redwood Inference, PM)
- Noah Patel (Redwood Inference, Serving Runtime)
- Priya Nair (Northbridge Analytics, Platform Engineering Lead)
- James Liu (Northbridge Analytics, Staff ML Engineer)
- Elena Petrova (Northbridge Analytics, SRE)

---

[00:00] Colin O'Donnell: Alright, I think we’re live. Priya, James, Elena — good to see you again. This is our weekly POC check-in. We wanted to focus today on the tuning you tried last week and the rollback ask.

[00:12] Priya Nair: Yep. Thanks. We… we did some config changes on the Optimize side, mostly batching and caching. We got cost improvements, but we also saw a pretty nasty p95 regression in EU.

[00:24] Colin O'Donnell: Got it. Maybe quick round of intros for Noah and Paula, since they haven’t met Elena.

[00:30] Paula Mendes: Hi everyone, Paula, PM on rollouts and rollback workflows. I’m here mostly to hear the requirements and also what’s blocking you for POC-to-procurement.

[00:39] Noah Patel: Hey, Noah. I’m on the runtime side — config application, the apply pipeline, that sort of thing.

[00:46] Elena Petrova: Hi, Elena. SRE at Northbridge. I’ve been staring at the dashboards for the last three days.

[00:51] (crosstalk)

[00:52] Colin O'Donnell: Great. So Priya, do you want to walk us through what you changed and what you observed? And like, timestamps help if you have them.

[01:03] Priya Nair: Sure. So baseline, we were running… uh, the hosted endpoint in us-east-1 and eu-west-1. Same model, same traffic split. We turned on more aggressive continuous batching — I think your field was max_batch_tokens? — and we also toggled the prefix cache. Maybe it’s called KV cache. Sorry, I’m mixing terms.

[01:22] Noah Patel: That’s fine. We have both, but the user-facing one is “prefix cache” in the console. Internally it’s KV-prefill reuse.

[01:30] Priya Nair: Right. So after turning it on, cost per 1k tokens went down like… 18-ish percent for the same workload. But p95 went from 420ms to like 900ms. And then we started seeing some timeouts.

[01:46] Elena Petrova: Timeouts and 5xx. Not a ton, like 0.4% peak, but enough to trip our internal alert.

[01:53] Colin O'Donnell: And that was only in EU?

[01:55] Elena Petrova: Mostly EU. US was stable. Which is why we think maybe we messed up scoping. Or there’s some regional capacity difference.

[02:05] James Liu: Also the shape of traffic in EU is different. We do more long-context there, I think. That’s our finance users.

[02:14] Noah Patel: Okay, that’s a big clue. The cache can increase memory pressure depending on prefix reuse patterns and sequence lengths. If EU has longer prompts and less reuse, it can actually make things worse.

[02:26] Priya Nair: That makes sense. But then the second issue was: we tried to roll it back. And it took… too long. Like we didn’t know if it actually applied. We basically reverted the toggle and waited.

[02:38] Elena Petrova: We were also nervous it was partially applied. Like maybe some workers still had the old values.

[02:44] Colin O'Donnell: Yep. This is exactly what we’re trying to solve with versioning + safe apply + rollback. Paula, do you want to frame what’s coming, and then we can map it to what they need in POC?

[02:55] Paula Mendes: Sure. So today, the experience is: you change optimization settings, it’s kind of “live,” and it can be hard to answer: what changed, who changed it, how to revert precisely. The project we’re building introduces immutable config versions with metadata, then a staged apply workflow, and a rollback button that reverts to a prior known-good version.

[03:16] Priya Nair: That’s exactly what we want. And honestly procurement is asking for it. Like audit trail + RBAC.

[03:23] Paula Mendes: Yep. We can go deeper on the audit and permissions in a second.

[03:28] Colin O'Donnell: For the POC: we can do a manual “pin to version” kind of thing today, but it’s not one-click in the UI yet. We can talk about what’s realistic.

[03:39] James Liu: Before we go there, can I just clarify something? The batching change, is that global for the model? Or per region? Because we thought we were applying EU only.

[03:49] Colin O'Donnell: Good question. Today the console scope can be confusing. It depends on whether you applied at “deployment” vs “model route.” I don’t want to guess — Elena, do you know what you clicked?

[04:00] Elena Petrova: I have the screenshot. It said “Route: /v1/chat completions” and then model. I picked EU region in a dropdown, I’m pretty sure.

[04:10] Noah Patel: If you picked region explicitly, it should scope. But we’ve seen cases where people think they picked a sub-scope and they actually applied at the higher scope. Paula, is that one of the UX bugs?

[04:20] Paula Mendes: Yeah, the current UX doesn’t always summarize blast radius well. In the new flow, the confirmation will say: tenant X, models Y, regions Z, percent canary, estimated affected QPS.

[04:35] Priya Nair: That would help a lot. Right now it’s like… “Apply changes?” and you’re like, uh, yes? Maybe?

[04:43] Colin O'Donnell: Understood.

[04:45] Noah Patel: For the regression: can you share the exact values you changed? Like max batch tokens and any queue delay.

[04:52] James Liu: We set max batch tokens from 2k to 6k. And we increased… there’s a “batching window,” we set it to 18ms. It was 8ms before.

[05:05] Noah Patel: Okay. That’s aggressive. For long prompts, the queueing component might dominate.

[05:11] Elena Petrova: We were following the recs from the Optimize tool. It suggested that.

[05:15] Colin O'Donnell: Yeah, the suggestions assume a certain distribution. If your EU traffic is long-context, it can backfire.

[05:23] Priya Nair: Right. So requirement wise: we need to be able to try these suggestions, but if it goes sideways we need to revert fast. Like minutes, not hours.

[05:34] Paula Mendes: When you say “revert fast,” is it: (a) revert the config immediately, (b) ensure all workers converge, and (c) have a status indicator? Or is “I clicked rollback” enough?

[05:47] Elena Petrova: We need status. Because during incident, we need to say “rollback in progress, 70% done,” that sort of thing. Also want to ensure no mixed state.

[05:58] Noah Patel: Mixed state is tricky in distributed systems but we can make it safe. The new applier treats it as a transaction with checkpoints, and we track applied version per worker group.

[06:11] James Liu: But does that mean it drains connections? Like if you roll back, do you kill pods?

[06:17] Noah Patel: Not necessarily. Some changes require cache invalidation, which can cause a transient latency bump. We’re trying to do it in a controlled way — like step down caches rather than hard flush.

[06:28] Priya Nair: Okay, but during our incident we don’t care if there’s a small bump. We care that p95 doesn’t stay doubled.

[06:36] Colin O'Donnell: Makes sense.

[06:39] Paula Mendes: Another question: do you want rollback scoped to region only, or can it be tenant-wide? Some customers want both, but RBAC differs.

[06:48] Priya Nair: Both. But default should be narrow. Like only the scope you changed.

[06:55] Elena Petrova: And please don’t let me roll back US by accident.

[06:59] Paula Mendes: Yep, we’re aligned.

[07:02] Colin O'Donnell: Let’s talk about what happened operationally. Elena, when you reverted, how long did it take for metrics to recover?

[07:10] Elena Petrova: About 20 minutes to see p95 back down. But we didn’t know when the change actually propagated. It could’ve been 2 minutes or 18.

[07:23] Noah Patel: That’s consistent with cache state + batching queue effects. Even after applying, there’s some inertia.

[07:32] James Liu: Also we had a weird thing where response headers looked different. We couldn’t tell if we were hitting the new config.

[07:39] Colin O'Donnell: That’s another feature we’re adding — optionally surfacing active config version in response headers. It’s behind a flag, but for debugging it’s super helpful.

[07:50] Priya Nair: Yes please. That would’ve saved us.

[07:55] Paula Mendes: It’s on the roadmap. For the POC, we can probably enable it for your account, depending on timing.

[08:03] Noah Patel: I want to ask about your success criteria. You said 18% cost improvement but p95 doubled. What’s the acceptable p95 for you?

[08:12] Priya Nair: Under 500ms for our main endpoint, with occasional spikes. p99 is allowed to be like 1.5s. But p95 at 900ms breaks UX.

[08:23] Elena Petrova: And 5xx needs to stay under 0.1%. We have a hard SLO with customers.

[08:30] Noah Patel: Great. Those map directly to the gates we’re implementing: 5xx, p95/p99. We also look at saturation: GPU util, queue depth, OOM events.

[08:42] James Liu: Do you also gate quality? Like if we try quantization, we need to ensure outputs don’t degrade.

[08:49] Paula Mendes: For quantization specifically, yes. There will be an optional eval gate in canary — you can run your prompt set and compare metrics. In early GA we might require manual confirmation depending on noise.

[09:02] Priya Nair: We’re not doing quantization yet, but we will. Procurement asked “how do you ensure model quality doesn’t regress,” so we need a story.

[09:12] Colin O'Donnell: Understood. We can provide a written description and our planned flow.

[09:18] Elena Petrova: Also the audit log. We need to show: who made the change, when, and what exactly. Our security team is like, “show me the diff.”

[09:28] Paula Mendes: Yep. The new config objects have immutable versions, with a diff view in console. Audit events will include old_version and new_version, actor identity, scope, and request ID.

[09:41] Priya Nair: Will it integrate with SIEM? We export logs to Splunk.

[09:45] Paula Mendes: Yes, we’ll emit structured audit events. Retention in our platform depends on your plan, but export can be continuous.

[09:54] James Liu: Can we get those events during the POC?

[09:57] Paula Mendes: We can get you some audit event examples and potentially enable the stream. I need to check with Security on what’s ready for external.

[10:07] Noah Patel: Back to the regression: James, you mentioned EU has longer prompts. Do you have a distribution? Average tokens in, tokens out.

[10:16] James Liu: Roughly 2.5k in, 400 out in EU. In US it’s like 800 in, 250 out.

[10:26] Noah Patel: Yeah, that’s significant. Batching window of 18ms can cause a big queue for those long prefill operations.

[10:36] Colin O'Donnell: So likely fix is: different settings per region, plus a safer canary. Which ties into versioning.

[10:43] Priya Nair: Exactly. We’d like to canary, like 10% of EU traffic.

[10:48] Paula Mendes: Perfect. The safe apply flow supports percent canary at the scope. For today’s POC we can emulate by splitting traffic on your side, but I know that’s annoying.

[11:00] Elena Petrova: We can split traffic, but then you get mixed metrics and it’s hard to interpret. We’d rather you do it.

[11:08] Paula Mendes: Understood.

[11:10] Colin O'Donnell: For timeline, we’re targeting limited GA Feb/March. This call is Jan 14, so for your POC we can do manual controls, but the full one-click might not land in time. That said, we can prioritize enabling a “revert to prior config” endpoint for select accounts.

[11:29] Priya Nair: The procurement timeline is end of Feb. So if you can show something by then, that helps.

[11:36] Paula Mendes: That aligns.

[11:38] James Liu: What’s the semantics of rollback? Like, if we changed three fields, rollback reverts all three? Or can we revert one?

[11:47] Paula Mendes: Rollback is version-based, so it reverts to the previous version exactly. It’s not field-level. We do show a diff so you can understand what’s changing.

[11:59] Priya Nair: That’s fine. We just need to get back to known good.

[12:04] Elena Petrova: Also please make it idempotent. Like if I click twice, don’t make it worse.

[12:10] Noah Patel: Yes. Idempotent and safe retries is a core requirement. Also we’re putting safeguards for race conditions — apply and rollback won’t interleave.

[12:22] Priya Nair: We literally had two people trying to “fix it” at once. That’s real life.

[12:27] Colin O'Donnell: Yep.

[12:29] James Liu: Another question: we want to restrict who can do this. Like only SRE on-call. But product engineers should be able to propose a config.

[12:40] Paula Mendes: That maps to RBAC roles: create vs apply vs rollback. We’re adding an “optimization change operator” role.

[12:49] Elena Petrova: And approvals? Like can we require a second person?

[12:54] Paula Mendes: For initial GA, we’ll support role-based restriction, but not full two-person approval workflow out of the box. Some customers implement approvals via webhook + internal tooling.

[13:06] Priya Nair: That might be okay for now.

[13:08] Colin O'Donnell: You mentioned confusion about scope. Can you describe what you expected to happen when you applied?

[13:15] Priya Nair: We expected EU-only change. But then we saw some mild blip in US too, and we weren’t sure if it was correlated.

[13:24] Elena Petrova: It could be noise. But since we don’t have version headers, we can’t prove it.

[13:30] Noah Patel: Right. If we can enable “config version in header,” it becomes obvious.

[13:36] Colin O'Donnell: We’ll try to do that.

[13:38] Paula Mendes: For the future UI, the rollback confirmation will show “blast radius summary” and you’ll type to confirm. That reduces fat-finger.

[13:49] Priya Nair: Thank you.

[13:51] James Liu: We also want a diff that highlights risky fields. Like batching window changes should show “risk: latency.”

[13:59] Paula Mendes: That’s in design. Fields will be tagged with risk categories.

[14:06] Noah Patel: On runtime side, we’ll also do semantic validation. Like if you set max_batch_tokens too high relative to GPU memory, we can block it.

[14:17] Priya Nair: Good. But we need override sometimes.

[14:21] Noah Patel: There will be overrides with elevated permissions, but we try to prevent obvious footguns.

[14:28] Elena Petrova: Can you also pause a rollout? Like if canary is going bad, don’t auto-progress.

[14:35] Paula Mendes: Yes. Safe apply can pause and requires confirmation to proceed past gates.

[14:43] Colin O'Donnell: Okay. Let’s zoom into the incident timeline. Elena, when did you apply the change?

[14:50] Elena Petrova: Jan 9, around 14:20 UTC. We saw p95 trending up within five minutes.

[14:58] James Liu: And then we reverted around 14:40 UTC.

[15:02] Elena Petrova: We declared a minor incident internally. Not Sev-1 but… it was close.

[15:09] Noah Patel: If you can send the request ID range or trace IDs from that window, I can correlate with runtime logs. Even just a sample of 20.

[15:20] Elena Petrova: We can. Our traces are in Datadog.

[15:23] Colin O'Donnell: Perfect.

[15:25] Priya Nair: One more thing: we need to communicate to our leadership that Redwood is taking change management seriously. Because they compare you to Bedrock, where we can just swap endpoints.

[15:37] Colin O'Donnell: Yeah, we hear that. Our differentiation is we give you deeper knobs, but that comes with safety tooling. That’s why we’re building this.

[15:48] James Liu: Together also has “roll back,” but it’s kind of manual.

[15:52] Colin O'Donnell: Understood.

[15:55] Paula Mendes: For procurement, what exact artifacts do they want? SOC2, audit logs, RBAC docs?

[16:02] Priya Nair: They want: RBAC and audit log spec, plus a statement about rollback for production changes. Like “you can revert quickly.”

[16:14] Elena Petrova: And they asked if we have a runbook.

[16:18] Paula Mendes: We will have a rollback runbook. For now, we can share a draft of the operator procedure we recommend.

[16:26] Noah Patel: Just to be clear, today, rollback is basically “apply previous settings,” which is not transactional. So we need to position it as “manual revert” vs “one-click rollback.”

[16:38] Colin O'Donnell: Yes. We’ll be careful.

[16:41] Priya Nair: That’s fine, as long as we have something for POC and a roadmap commitment.

[16:49] Paula Mendes: We can provide the roadmap milestone and what’s included in limited GA. We do not want to overpromise.

[16:57] James Liu: On the quality side, we can give you a prompt set. It’s not huge. Like 30 prompts.

[17:05] Paula Mendes: Perfect. That’s a good start for canary eval gate, especially later for quantization.

[17:12] Noah Patel: Also: in EU, you might want to reduce batching window and cap max batch tokens. We can suggest initial values based on your distribution.

[17:24] Priya Nair: But we still want cache if it helps.

[17:27] Noah Patel: Right. Cache should be selectively enabled where reuse exists. If your prompts are mostly unique, it’s wasted memory.

[17:37] James Liu: We can measure reuse. We have repeating system prompts but user content differs.

[17:42] Noah Patel: System prompt reuse does help, but only if the system prefix is identical and long enough. If it’s short, benefit is small.

[17:54] Colin O'Donnell: Okay. Let’s cover “what would good look like” for rollback. Priya, imagine the ideal.

[18:02] Priya Nair: Ideal is: we can make a change, it creates a version. We apply to EU 10% canary. We watch p95, 5xx, GPU util. If it fails, we click rollback and it goes back. And we can show auditors: version 12 was applied by James, rollback by Elena at time X.

[18:22] Elena Petrova: And it shouldn’t take 20 minutes to even start. It should start immediately.

[18:28] Noah Patel: Start immediately, yes. Full recovery depends on state (cache), but we can reflect progress.

[18:37] Paula Mendes: Also “one click” includes guardrails: it will show you the blast radius and ask you to confirm.

[18:45] James Liu: Also API. We’d like API access, not only UI.

[18:50] Paula Mendes: Yes, there will be an endpoint to rollback to a previous version.

[18:56] Priya Nair: Great.

[18:58] Colin O'Donnell: One more thing: do you need this for private deployment? I know you’re hosted today.

[19:04] Priya Nair: Not now, but later we might need VPC or on-prem. Our healthcare customers ask about it.

[19:11] Colin O'Donnell: Understood.

[19:13] Elena Petrova: But the change management story should be same across modes.

[19:17] Paula Mendes: Exactly. The version model is consistent across hosted, dedicated, and private.

[19:24] Noah Patel: Okay. Next, I want to confirm: the regression could also be from a cache invalidation event when you toggled. Did you see a spike right at apply time?

[19:36] Elena Petrova: Yes, there was a spike. But then it stayed high.

[19:41] Noah Patel: So likely combination: immediate spike from state change, then sustained because of queueing.

[19:50] James Liu: That sounds right.

[19:52] Colin O'Donnell: Alright. Let’s do next steps and owners. Elena will send metrics and screenshots before/after, plus the exact apply time. James will send prompt set. Noah will investigate and propose safe defaults and a canary plan. Paula will send a roadmap and documentation around rollback/audit. Sound good?

[20:14] Priya Nair: Yes.

[20:15] Elena Petrova: Yes.

[20:17] James Liu: Yep.

[20:18] Paula Mendes: Works.

[20:20] Colin O'Donnell: Before we wrap, any open questions on the rollback implementation? Like semantics.

[20:26] Elena Petrova: If a rollout is half-applied and then I rollback, do you guarantee it converges to the rolled-back version?

[20:34] Noah Patel: The goal is yes. We treat rollback as a new desired version and the controller reconciles. There are edge cases today, but we’re fixing those specifically — preventing mixed worker states.

[20:48] Priya Nair: Can you send us that in writing? That’s what leadership asks.

[20:52] Paula Mendes: We can write the intended semantics, plus what’s available now.

[20:57] James Liu: And please include whether the rollback is idempotent.

[21:01] Noah Patel: Yes.

[21:03] Colin O'Donnell: Great. We’ll follow up by email. Thanks everyone.

[21:08] (Call continues with light scheduling / calendar coordination)

[21:15] Colin O'Donnell: Let’s find time Friday or Monday for a 30-minute technical follow-up once Noah has looked at the data.

[21:21] Priya Nair: Monday is better.

[21:23] Colin O'Donnell: Cool, we’ll send.

---

Auto-generated Notes (Fireflies)
- Key moment: Regression after enabling cache + more aggressive batching, especially for longer-context EU traffic.
- Primary ask: one-click rollback with version history, diff, RBAC, and audit trail; ability to canary by percent and gate on p95/5xx.
- Risk: scope confusion (region/model) and lack of visibility into active config version.
